name: Copy rule is fault-bounding
summary: n separate |+⟩-states are fault-bounded by a Z-state plugged into an n-legged X-spider.
description: The ordinary [copy rule](../state-copy/) is not fault-equivalent, but it can only improve fault tolerance: the $n$ separate one-legged Z-spiders on the left are *fault-bounded* by the right-hand side, meaning every fault on the left has a fault of at most the same weight with the same effect on the right (any flip on a boundary edge on the left is the same flip on the right). The converse fails, since a single flip on the internal edge on the right spreads to all $n$ legs. So applying the copy rule from right to left, to remove a spider, never makes a diagram less fault-tolerant. The colour-swapped version holds as well.
conditions: Fault boundedness only (left is fault-bounded by right), not fault equivalence.

source.location: App. C.4, lemma on the copy rule

parameter_notes: n outputs (shown for n = 3); holds for any n ≥ 1.
